brandText.brandText: A social handle becomes the payment destination.

strategyText.strategyText: Reply under the post, mention TweetSend with an amount, confirm. That is the whole flow.

strategyHeading.strategyHeading: Wallet addresses are hard to remember, easy to mistype, and nowhere near the conversation

processText.processText: Find wallet, copy address, open wallet, paste address, verify network, send. TweetSend replaces all of it with a reply and a confirm.

processHeading.processHeading: Six steps collapse into one reply and one confirmation

teamText.teamText: Five steps, and only the first one happens on X.

description.description: You see a post from someone you want to pay. You reply to it with the bot mention and an amount, for example @TweetSend $50. That is the entire instruction: no address, no network picker, no second app.

TweetSend detects the reply through the X API and identifies the author of the tweet you replied to. You never have to type the recipient's wallet address, or even their handle - the thread already says who it is for.
The bot returns a secure confirmation link. You connect a wallet or use your existing TweetSend balance, pick the supported asset and network if there is a choice, and sign the payment.

If the recipient already uses TweetSend, the funds go to their linked wallet. If they have never used it, the payment stays claimable for that X account instead of sitting at an address nobody has verified.

The recipient signs in with X, proves ownership of the same account the payment was addressed to, and claims the funds to a wallet they control. The bot can report the payment as pending, completed, claimed, expired or refunded along the way.

advisorsNotableInvestors.name: Do I need the recipient's wallet address?

bio.raw: {"nodeType":"document","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"No. TweetSend identifies the author of the tweet you replied to and uses that verified X account as the destination. No wallet address has to be posted publicly and no QR code has to be scanned. Wallets still exist underneath - you just interact with @handles instead of long hexadecimal addresses. The product rule is that you should never have to trust a random wallet address pasted into a reply: the verified social identity is the destination you recognise, and the wallet routing happens beneath it.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}

advisorsNotableInvestors.name: What if the recipient has never used TweetSend?

bio.raw: {"nodeType":"document","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"paragraph","data":{},"content":[{"nodeType":"text","value":"The payment stays claimable for that X account. When they sign in with X and prove ownership of the same account, TweetSend matches the payment to the verified identity and lets them claim it to a wallet they control. Until that happens the funds wait in a claimable flow rather than at an address nobody has checked, and the bot can reply under the thread to say the money is waiting for them.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}

advisorsNotableInvestors.name: What does the bot actually reply with?

Reply @TweetSend $25 under a post and the bot answers \"Payment ready. Confirm your $25 send.\" Once it settles it answers \"$25 sent to @recipient.\" If the recipient has not joined yet it answers \"$25 is waiting for @recipient. They can claim it by signing in with X.\" Payments can also report as pending, completed, claimed, expired or refunded, and the site keeps the full history of what you sent, received, claimed and had refunded.","marks":[],"data":{}}]}]}
